cases.C16: Imprimatur turns human approval into a memorable, authoritative promise: apt for governed AI. Its ecclesiastical flavour is niche, while clear UK registration and four relevant domains support credibility.
cases.C11: Cautia makes caution feel concise and ownable, with a sober, trust-oriented sound for enterprise buyers. Pronunciation and the Cautio proximity need checking, but its clear registration and available .co.uk/.io help.
cases.C24: Claustra names exactly what you're selling: gates that open only on approval. Clean registry, full domain set, no security-brand collision—claustrophobia echo just reinforces controlled access.
cases.C25: Runnymede uniquely grounds AI containment in Magna Carta's iconic constitutional power-limiting heritage; 'Labs' clearly distinguishes it from the race-equality trust, delivering instant gravitas to UK enterprise buyers.
cases.C31: As Roman fortification infrastructure enforcing strict perimeter control, Vallum perfectly embodies an architecture of distrust; pairing it with 'Labs' cleanly establishes a distinct commercial identity for UK enterprise clients.
cases.C30: Provost Labs sounds institutional but precisely names delegated, checkable authority—agents act only with granted powers. The academic echo reinforces governance, sobriety, and trust, while domains and Companies House are clear.
cases.C15: Countermand captures the exact CISO promise: humans can revoke risky AI orders. Military gravitas is sober, not gung-ho; no clashes, and all four domains are free.
cases.C18: Redoubt’s fortification image precisely frames contained agents and approval gates. Survivalist fringe is distant; obscure security names don’t own the concept. Exact domains are taken, so secure a prefixed domain.
cases.C29: Seneschal literally means steward holding delegated power within strict grant—our architecture. Archaic gravitas reads as CISO-grade seriousness; one-time spelling hurdle yields a memorable, distinctive, unowned name.
cases.C22: Bailiwick literally means rightful jurisdiction—the agent principle embodied. Jersey's regulated-finance reputation reassures CISOs and CFOs. The Fortune 500 collision is in unrelated managed-IT services, not software.
cases.C27: Anchorite means 'walled in by choice' — metaphor for capability containment, human-in-the-loop risk, need-to-know data flow. 'Labs' signals rigor. Monastic = discipline, not isolation. Distinct from shield/guard names. No AI conflict.
cases.C12: Veto Labs directly mirrors the core “human‑in‑the‑loop” promise, instantly conveying block‑action authority to CISOs. Its brevity, clear domains, and non‑political branding outweigh the minor overlap with veto.so.
cases.C26: Chary perfectly encodes the architecture of distrust. Its rarity creates a distinctive, intellectual brand, while "Labs" anchors it firmly in tech, preventing any confusion with "charity."
cases.C17: A masterclass in delegated authority. Its literary weight mirrors Palantir, commanding respect from CISOs. The domain hurdle is small compared to the prestige of this high-status identity.
cases.C23: Penstock's flow-metering metaphor perfectly embodies distrust architecture. Pentera sound-alike risk is minor—different markets, different users recognize the distinction immediately. Registrable, memorable, sober.
cases.C14: Vouchsafe captures earned trust elegantly, but the UK biometric startup (vouchsafe.id) creates real confusion in identity/access control conversations. The archaic register also risks being perceived as evasive rather than precise.
